He.ie_source: https://physics.nist.gov/cgi-bin/ASD/ie.pl (NIST ASD, eV, accessed 2026-09-02; raw TSV archived as nist_ie_*.tsv)
reactivity_facts: No neutral covalent compound isolated in bulk; only endohedral complexes He@C60 (Saunders et al., Science 259:1428, 1993) and ions like HeH+ observed; Na2He high-pressure phase confirmed (2017)

Ne.ie_source: https://physics.nist.gov/cgi-bin/ASD/ie.pl (NIST ASD, eV, accessed 2026-09-02; raw TSV archived as nist_ie_*.tsv)
reactivity_facts: No stable neutral/covalent neon compounds known under any pressure or temperature (Lewars, Modelling Marvels, Springer 2008, pp.70-71); [B12(CN)11Ne]- predicted (RSC Chem. Commun. 2020) but not confirmed - Neon is the only noble gas with no definitively confirmed compound

Ar.ie_source: https://physics.nist.gov/cgi-bin/ASD/ie.pl (NIST ASD, eV, accessed 2026-09-02; raw TSV archived as nist_ie_*.tsv)
reactivity_facts: Chemically inert under most conditions; forms no confirmed stable compounds at room temperature (Argon page)
HArF (argon fluorohydride) synthesized in low-temperature matrix, announced 2000 (Khriachtchev et al., Nature 406:874, doi:10.1038/35022551) - stable only in cryogenic matrices

Kr.ie_source: https://physics.nist.gov/cgi-bin/ASD/ie.pl (NIST ASD, eV, accessed 2026-09-02; raw TSV archived as nist_ie_*.tsv)
reactivity_facts: KrF2 (krypton difluoride) first krypton compound, reported 1963 (Grosse et al., Science 139:1047); synthesized from Kr + F2 under extreme forcing conditions (electric discharge/low temperature photolysis)
KrF2 crystal structure determined (Burbank et al., Science 178:1285, 1972); decomposes at ~-20C or below 0C depending on source - thermodynamically unstable

Xe.ie_source: https://physics.nist.gov/cgi-bin/ASD/ie.pl (NIST ASD, eV, accessed 2026-09-02; raw TSV archived as nist_ie_*.tsv)
reactivity_facts: XeF2: photochemical synthesis Xe + F2 under UV (Weeks, Chernick, Matheson, JACS 84:4612, 1962)
XeF4: first binary noble-gas compound via Xe+F2 at high temperature (Claassen, Selig, Malm, JACS 84:3593, 1962)
XeF6: from XeF2 heating with NiF2 catalyst (Tramsek & Zemva 2006)
First noble gas compound: Xe+[PtF6]- (Bartlett, Proc. Chem. Soc. 1962), triggered by IE(Xe)=1170 kJ/mol ~ IE(O2)=1165 kJ/mol
Also XeO3, XeO4, XeO2 known; classified 'relatively reactive' group (IE 12.1 eV)

Rn.ie_source: https://physics.nist.gov/cgi-bin/ASD/ie.pl (NIST ASD, eV, accessed 2026-09-02; raw TSV archived as nist_ie_*.tsv)
reactivity_facts: RnF2 (radon difluoride) formed by oxidation with F2; also [RnF]+[Sb2F11]- from Rn + [O2]+[SbF6]-; RnO3 reported (Stein 1983/2010 studies)
Not chemically inert, but 3.8 d half-life of 222Rn makes chemistry difficult; reactivity inferred and only a few compounds reported (all fluorides/oxides)
Classified 'relatively reactive' group (IE 10.7 eV); predicted most metallic noble gas
